To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the temperature and entropy of black holes, as well as the rate of evaporation, are subject to corrections due to the generalized uncertainty principle, and that these corrections increase the temperature, decrease the entropy, and speed up the decay of the black hole.

the Hawking radiation of TeV-scale black hole is subject to two corrections: (1) the generalized uncertainty principle, which results in a higher temperature and a lower entropy, and (2) thermal fluctuations of the black hole's horizon, which results in an even higher temperature and a still lower entropy.
the entropy and temperature of black holes are modified by the presence of the GUP and thermal fluctuations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how classical are black holes.

the following questions: (1) How do black holes behave in quantum gravity? (2) What can we learn from the properties of quantum black holes? (3) Can black holes be produced at the Large Hadron Collider? (4) What can we expect from quantum black holes produced in future colliders? (5) What are the prospects for observing quantum black holes in the future?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the classicality of black holes is a matter of degree.
the classical picture of black holes is not applicable in the TeV range, and the production cross-section of black holes at future colliders is expected to be much smaller than the naive estimate.
the black hole evaporation is not a classical phenomenon, even if the black hole mass is of the order of the Planck mass.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TeV-scale black hole evaporation is a very interesting and promising process.
the Hawking evaporation of TeV-scale black hole would be faster than what is usually believed.
the black holes produced in colliders are not as classical as one might have expected.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the classical picture of black holes may not be appropriate in such a setting.
black holes are less 'black', i.e., less classical and more quantum, at higher energies.
the black hole lifetime is reduced by a factor of order unity, and its entropy is reduced by a larger factor.
